title: Algiers musicians: McCurdy, Pierron, Boccage and George Field
summary: The McCurdy boys, Pierron, the boat-building Boccage family and George Field are discussed as Algiers musicians.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you ever hear Bab Frank?
No. Maybe I forgot about that.
Do you remember the Peerless band, McCurdy and...
McCurdy's, McCurdy's boys, eh? Mm-hmm. Well, wait, let me tell you.
The fellow worked with him on piccolo too, Bab Frank, I think.
Yeah. Charlie McCurdy's boys, yeah. Charlie McCurdy's boys, boys, yeah, he from Algeys too. I'm not sure, I don't remember. I know they used to have some McCurdy's from Algeys students to play music.
Who all was over there in Algeys when you were a youngster? The musicians?

Who all was over there? That's why the, Pierron, them come from over there. Pierron's come from there? Yeah, Pierron from over there. Pierron, I think he used to have a brother too play music. Because they used to come across on the ferry all the time at night.
Peter Boccage? Yeah, they come from over there too. I mean, Peter Boccage make boats.
Oh yeah, that's right, I heard that.
Yeah, they make boats. You know, they like all them fishing boats and them race boats. That's what they do too.
Well, how big is that family? That's that one of them.
Ooh, that must be a mighty big family.
Well, there was another trombonist used to play with them. I wonder if you remember George Field?
I heard talk of George Field. Well, you see them fellas.
Yeah, you see them fellas, you could hardly keep up with some of them. You may see them now and don't see them no more for a year or so.
